newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sogaris says new CDG extension fully-let.
newsitem.headline: Sogaris says new CDG extension fully-let.

text.p: French freight installations operator, Sogaris, said a further two companies had rented space in the two-building extension to its Centre Logistique de Fret Aerien (CLFA), at Paris-Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport.
The CLFA extension, which opened at the start of May and cost 60 million francs to develop, provides an extra 10,000 sq m of warehousing and 2,200 sq m of office space.

"Airfreight agents, Air Express International (AEI), which already occupied 3,600 sq m of warehousing at the site has taken an additional 900 sq m as well as 210 sq m of offices," a Sogaris official told Reuters.

The French unit of Dutch forwarding group, Miro, whose existing rehousing facilities at the CLFA cover 1,200 sq m, is occupying an extra 450 sq metres in the extension and 105 sq metres of offices, the official said.

Sogaris had already signed up Air France Industries, the aircraft maintenance division of the Air France up Federal Express Corp and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV services subsidiary, Cargo Service Centre (CSC), to occupy space in the extension boosting overall capacity the site to 28,000 sq m of warehousing and 7,000 sq m of offices , the Sogaris official added.
"We are now concentrating on third-phase development in the form of a 6,300 sq. m building to enter service in July 1998 for which demand from potential tenants is already strong."
A longer-term objective is for the CLFA complex to be extended to cover 62,000 sq. metres, wholly- dedicated to airfreight activities, the Sogaris official said.
Sogaris is 80 percent-owned by public authorities in the Paris area with the remaining 20 percent owned by private investors. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
